selected_evidence.summary: Captured pre-change boot_id (cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64), current /proc/cmdline (no audit=1), grubby info, and /etc/default/grub contents.

grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" applied to BLS entry (verified via grubby --info=ALL and /boot/loader/entries/*.conf), and GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub updated to include audit=1 without duplication.
Issued sudo shutdown -r now on node1; exec stream closed as the node went down, acknowledging the restart command before disconnection.

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving genuine restart
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id changed from cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64 (pre-restart) to cd5e4eb8-4f29-4bb7-8197-f756bb31e5c7 (post-restart), and connectivity was lost then restored, proving an actual reboot occurred.
Post-reboot /proc/cmdline shows 'audit=1' appended to the kernel command line, confirming the setting survived the reboot.

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "STEP 1: add audit=1 via grubby to all kernels"
sudo -n grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1"

echo "STEP 2: persist in /etc/default/grub for GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX"
sudo -n cp /etc/default/grub /etc/default/grub.bak
if grep -q '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' /etc/default/grub; then
  sudo -n sed -i 's/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="\(.*\)"/GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="\1 audit=1"/' /etc/default/grub
fi
grep '^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX' /etc/default/grub

echo "STEP 3: verify grubby info shows audit=1 for all kernel entries"
sudo -n grubby --info=ALL | grep -E 'args|kernel='

echo "STEP 4: verify BLS entry files on disk"
sudo -n grep -H audit=1 /boot/loader/entries/*.conf || true

echo "STEP 5: confirm current live cmdline (will update after reboot)"
cat /proc/cmdline
